document_text:
# Kasa Software – Company and Product Brief

Launch of the Fakturo invoicing and tax app in Italy. Internal document for the launch planning team. All companies, people and figures in this document are fictional and used for evaluation only.

## 1. Company overview

Kasa Software sp. z o.o. is a Polish software company founded in 2016 in Kraków by Anna Wiśniewska and Piotr Zając, two former tax consultants. It builds invoicing and bookkeeping apps for freelancers and very small businesses.

In 2024 Kasa had 64 employees, 38,000 paying customers in Poland and a turnover of 7.8 million euros. Customers pay a monthly subscription; 4% of them cancel each month.

## 2. The product: Fakturo

Fakturo is a web and mobile app that creates electronic invoices, sends them to the national e-invoicing system and estimates the taxes the user will owe.

- Electronic invoices in the Italian FatturaPA format, sent to the Sistema di Interscambio (SdI).
- Tax estimate for the flat-rate regime (regime forfettario), updated with every invoice.
- Photo capture of receipts and expense tracking.
- Export for the accountant (commercialista).
- Price: 9 euros per month, or 90 euros per year. 30-day free trial.

The Italian version was tested in 2025 with 250 beta users: 68% were still active after 3 months, and the average rating was 4.4 out of 5. 41% of beta users asked for a feature to pay their tax instalments (F24) from the app, which is not yet available.

## 3. Why Italy, and launch goals

Italy made electronic invoicing mandatory for flat-rate freelancers in 2024, so many of them now need a tool they did not use before.

Goals for the Italian launch, approved by the board in July 2025:

- Reach 12,000 paying customers in Italy within 24 months.
- Keep monthly cancellations below 3%.
- Sign partnerships with at least 3 professional associations in the first year.

The launch is planned for January 2027, at the start of the tax year.

## 4. Market context

Figures from the report "Freelance software in Italy 2025" by Osservatorio DigitalWork and from the Freelance Barometer 2025 survey (both fictional sources for this evaluation).

| Indicator | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Freelancers with a VAT number (partita IVA) in Italy | 3.4 million | Osservatorio DigitalWork 2025 |
| Of which in the flat-rate regime | 1.9 million | Osservatorio DigitalWork 2025 |
| Flat-rate freelancers who use an invoicing app | 44% | Freelance Barometer 2025 |
| Average monthly price paid for an invoicing app | 7.20 euros | Freelance Barometer 2025 |

## 5. Customer groups

The Freelance Barometer 2025 measured interest in "an app that creates electronic invoices and estimates your taxes, at 9 euros per month" among freelancers with a VAT number.

| Group | Freelancers | Purchase intent |
|---|---|---|
| Flat-rate freelancers who do not use an invoicing app yet | 1.06 million | 23% |
| Flat-rate freelancers who already use an invoicing app | 0.84 million | 9% |
| Freelancers in the ordinary regime (with an accountant) | 1.5 million | 6% |
| Craft businesses with one owner (artigiani) | 0.9 million | 11% |

Freelancers who do not use an app today mostly use free tools from the tax agency or ask their accountant. 58% of them say they "do not understand how much tax they will owe".

## 6. Competitors

- **Fatture in Cloud**: market leader, broad features for small businesses, plans from 4 to 30 euros per month.
- **Agenzia delle Entrate free tool**: free, basic invoicing, no tax estimate.
- **Accountant-provided software**: often included in the accountant's fee.
- **Other freelance apps**: several smaller apps focused on the flat-rate regime, 5 to 12 euros per month.

## 7. Distribution and marketing

Fakturo will be sold online only: website, App Store and Google Play. Kasa is talking to two professional associations (one for designers, one for IT consultants) about member discounts. The marketing budget for the first year is 600,000 euros.

## 8. Open points

- Target group and positioning against the leader.
- Whether to keep the price at 9 euros or launch at a lower price.
- Launch campaign concept and channel plan.

analysis.market_overview: Italy made electronic invoicing mandatory for all flat-rate (forfettario) freelancers on 1 January 2024, whatever their revenue [S2, S16]. The document puts the market at 3.4M freelancers with a VAT number, of which 1.9M are in the flat-rate regime [S3]. 44% of flat-rate freelancers use an invoicing app, and the average price paid is 7.20 euros per month [S3]. Official data show a steady inflow of new flat-rate registrations: 242,529 in 2025, or 48.5% of new VAT numbers and up 3.9% on 2024 [S18]. The market is crowded and priced low. Fatture in Cloud is the leader. Its Forfettari plan costs 4 euros per month in year 1 and 8 euros per month after that [S6, S7]. The tax agency offers free tools [S15], and Aruba and Fattura24 start at 1 and 4 euros per month [S9]. Some competitors, such as ForfettApp and Fiscozen, already cover F24 payments [S11, S13], and Fakturo does not yet [S1]. Among the document's customer groups, flat-rate freelancers without an app show the highest purchase intent at 9 euros per month (23%) [S4]. The Fakturo beta had 68% of users still active after 3 months and a 4.4/5 rating [S1].

competitors.name: Fatture in Cloud (TeamSystem)
competitors.positioning: Market leader with broad invoicing features for small businesses and professionals. E-invoicing is included (sending, receiving, signing, storage), with a 30-day free trial. The Forfettari plan is aimed at flat-rate freelancers but is limited to 100 documents per year. The document says plans run from 4 to 30 euros per month; web sources list plans up to 51 euros.

competitors.name: Agenzia delle Entrate free e-invoicing service
competitors.positioning: Free official tools to prepare, send and store e-invoices. Basic invoicing with no tax estimate. Flat-rate freelancers without an app mostly use it or ask their accountant.

competitors.name: Aruba Fatturazione Elettronica
competitors.positioning: Easy-to-use e-invoicing described as well suited to flat-rate freelancers, with a demo version. Only a blog comparison supports this.

competitors.name: Fattura24
competitors.positioning: Simplified invoicing for professionals, with a 30-day free trial. Founded in 2011 and based in Rome.

competitors.name: Qonto
competitors.positioning: Business bank account that bundles e-invoicing. The Starter plan is free for eligible professionals and sole traders. Paid professional plans start at 9 euros per month + VAT, billed annually.

competitors.name: ForfettApp
competitors.positioning: App focused on flat-rate freelancers. It offers e-invoicing and stores paid F24 forms, tax returns, INPS payments and invoices, which covers the F24 need Fakturo lacks.

competitors.name: Fiscozen
competitors.positioning: Online accountant plus app for VAT-number holders. Annual plans include a dedicated accountant, unlimited e-invoices, expense management and F24 submission. It is a full-service alternative to a self-service app.

competitors.name: Il Commercialista Online
competitors.positioning: Remote accounting firm offering flat-rate management packages, a service alternative to invoicing apps.

customer_needs: Understand how much tax they will owe: 58% of flat-rate freelancers without an app say they do not understand it [S4]
Comply with mandatory e-invoicing through the SdI, since late or missing e-invoices carry penalties [S16]
Pay tax instalments by F24 from the same app: 41% of Fakturo beta users asked for this [S1]
Taxes (substitute tax and contributions) are paid by F24 with a balance and advance payments, so a tax tool needs to support this schedule [S17]
Low-cost or free tools: many non-app users rely on the tax agency's free tools or on their accountant [S4]
Prices around the market average of 7.20 euros per month [S3]
Free trial before paying: competitors offer 30-day trials [S8]
Human or accountant support: online accountant services bundle a dedicated accountant [S13]

segments.label: Flat-rate freelancers without an app
segments.description: Flat-rate freelancers who do not yet use an invoicing app. 23% purchase intent for an app that creates e-invoices and estimates taxes at 9 euros per month [S4]. They mostly use the tax agency's free tools or ask their accountant, and 58% say they do not understand how much tax they will owe [S4]. E-invoicing became mandatory for them in 2024 [S2].
needs: Low price compared with free tools
Possibly F24 payment (requested by 41% of beta users) [S1]

segments.label: Flat-rate freelancers already using an app
segments.description: Flat-rate freelancers who already use an invoicing app. 9% purchase intent at 9 euros per month [S4]. They would have to switch from competitors priced from 4 to 8 euros per month (Fatture in Cloud) [S6].
needs: Price at or below current spend (average 7.20 euros per month) [S3]

segments.label: Ordinary-regime freelancers with an accountant
segments.description: Freelancers in the ordinary regime who work with an accountant. 6% purchase intent at 9 euros per month, the lowest of the four groups [S4].
needs: Invoicing integrated with the accountant's workflow

segments.label: One-owner craft businesses (artigiani)
segments.description: Craft businesses with one owner. 11% purchase intent at 9 euros per month [S4]. Online accountants sell separate plans for artisans and traders [S12].

data_quality_notes: The market figures (3.4M, 1.9M, 44%, 7.20 euros) and the customer-group sizes and purchase intent come from fictional sources named in the document (Osservatorio DigitalWork, Freelance Barometer). They could not be verified on the web.

The four customer groups add up to 4.3M, above the 3.4M VAT-number holders stated in the same document. The groups may overlap, or the artigiani may not be part of the 3.4M. Check the sizes before using them.
Purchase intent is stated interest at 9 euros per month, not actual purchases. It cannot be translated directly into customer numbers.
The beta test had only 250 users, so the retention (68%) and rating (4.4) figures are weak evidence.

Conflict on Fatture in Cloud pricing. The document says 4 to 30 euros per month, but web sources show plans up to 51 euros per month. The 4 euro Forfettari price applies only in year 1 and renews at 8 euros per month. A Shopify blog lists Fatture in Cloud from 8 euros per month.

Web prices come from pages dated 2026, and launch is planned for January 2027, so competitor prices may change. The Fatture in Cloud Forfettari plan has a limit of 100 documents per year, which may not suit all users [S8].
The prices for Aruba, Fattura24 and Libero SiFattura rest on a single blog comparison [S9]. Qonto's data comes from its own vendor blog [S10]. Both are weak sources.

The ForfettApp price was not found. The Fiscozen flat-rate price in the snippet was unclear, so both are marked unknown. The price level of Aruba and Fattura24 is assumed low from their 'from' prices only.
Accountant-provided software (document section 6, [S5]) and other small freelance apps (5 to 12 euros per month [S5]) are not named, so they are not listed as individual competitors.
No verified web figures were found for the size or growth of the invoicing-app market, nor on professional associations or how many flat-rate freelancers use an accountant.
The MEF data count new flat-rate registrations (233,511 in 2024; 242,529 in 2025) [S18]. They are not comparable with the document's stock of 1.9M flat-rate freelancers.

The claim that competitors cover F24 is based on the ForfettApp and Fiscozen pages only [S11, S13]. It was not checked whether they offer in-app payment or only storage and submission by an accountant.
The document's goals (12,000 customers in 24 months, cancellations below 3%) have no market benchmark in the sources [S2].

sources.reference: Company document, section 3 (Why Italy, and launch goals)

strategy.target_description: Flat-rate (forfettario) freelancers in Italy who do not yet use an invoicing app. Today they send e-invoices with the tax agency's free tools or rely on their accountant. They must issue e-invoices through the SdI, and most do not understand how much tax they will owe.
strategy.positioning_statement: For flat-rate freelancers still using free tools or their accountant, Fakturo is the invoicing app that shows how much tax you will owe, updated with every invoice. It also sends your e-invoices to the SdI. Unlike the tax agency's free tool, it gives a tax estimate. Unlike Fatture in Cloud, it is built for flat-rate freelancers and is not a broad small-business suite. Do not claim F24 payment, because the feature is not available yet.
strategy.value_proposition: Know your tax at every moment. Issue compliant e-invoices to the SdI and see a running tax estimate for the flat-rate regime, with receipt capture and an export for your accountant, in one app and with a 30-day free trial.
strategy.pricing_direction: Competitor prices are mixed. The agency tool is free. Fatture in Cloud Forfettari costs 4 euros per month in year 1 and 8 euros after that. The market average paid is 7.20 euros [S3, S6]. Do not try to undercut on price. Keep 9 euros per month, because the 23% purchase intent was measured at that price [S4]. Lead with the annual plan at 90 euros, which is 7.50 euros per month, close to the market average. Keep the 30-day free trial to match competitors. There is no evidence on demand at a lower price. If the team wants to test a lower launch price, run it as a limited A/B test in the first months. Re-check competitor prices before launch, because they may change by January 2027.
strategy.rationale: SEG1 is the largest and most interested segment. It has 1.06M freelancers and 23% stated purchase intent at 9 euros per month, which is about 244,000 people. This is stated interest, not purchases [S4]. The alternatives are weaker. SEG2 has 0.84M people at 9% (about 76,000) and would have to switch from competitors priced at 4 to 8 euros per month [S4, S6]. SEG3 has 1.5M people but only 6% intent (about 90,000) [S4]. SEG4 has 0.9M people at 11% (about 99,000) [S4]. SEG1 has roughly 2.5 to 3 times the intent-weighted pool of any other segment. The goal of 12,000 customers is about 1.1% of the SEG1 size, so the target looks reachable if the intent figures hold. That is my own calculation and not a market benchmark. Competition is also weaker here. These users mostly use the free agency tool or an accountant, and that tool has no tax estimate [S15]. E-invoicing has been mandatory for them since 2024 [S2, S16]. 58% say they do not understand their tax [S4], and Fakturo's live estimate answers that need. Because they often ask their accountant, accountant referrals and professional associations are the right channels. They also support the goal of 3 association partnerships. Risks: ForfettApp and Fiscozen appear to cover F24, but the sources do not confirm whether payment happens in the app [S11, S13]. 41% of beta users asked for F24 [S1], so it is a roadmap priority, and the launch must not promise it. The beta retention of 68% and rating of 4.4 come from only 250 users, so I do not use them as a headline claim. The segment sizes and intent come from unverified sources, and the four groups add up to more than the 3.4M total, so sizes may overlap. The channel mix is my assumption, because the analysis has no channel performance figures. The 600,000 euro budget split is still to be decided. Since 4% of customers cancel each month against a goal of under 3%, onboarding and the trial matter as much as acquisition.

campaign.concept: Every invoice answers the question flat-rate freelancers keep asking: "How much tax will I owe?" The campaign shows the tax estimate moving the moment an invoice is created, turning a vague worry into a number on the screen. This expresses the positioning: Fakturo is the invoicing app for flat-rate freelancers that shows the tax estimate with every invoice and also sends e-invoices to the SdI.
campaign.tagline: Ogni fattura ti mostra le tasse.

key_messages.headline: Partita IVA forfettaria? Le tasse, finalmente chiare.
key_messages.body: Fakturo è l'app di fatturazione pensata per i liberi professionisti in regime forfettario. Emette le fatture elettroniche e le invia al Sistema di Interscambio, e a ogni fattura aggiorna la stima delle tasse da pagare. Per i soci e le socie, 30 giorni di prova gratuita.

key_messages.headline: Il tuo commercialista riceve tutto già in ordine.
key_messages.body: Con Fakturo emetti le fatture elettroniche, fotografi gli scontrini e vedi la stima delle tasse del regime forfettario. Quando serve, esporti i dati per il tuo commercialista. Provala gratis per 30 giorni.

key_messages.headline: Fatture elettroniche e stima delle tasse in forfettario
key_messages.body: Invia le fatture al SdI e vedi quanto dovrai pagare, aggiornato a ogni fattura. Fakturo è fatta per chi è in regime forfettario. Prova gratis per 30 giorni, poi 9 € al mese o 90 € all'anno.

key_messages.headline: Hai appena emesso una fattura. Quanto dovrai di tasse?
key_messages.body: Con Fakturo lo vedi subito: la stima delle tasse del regime forfettario si aggiorna a ogni fattura, e la fattura elettronica parte verso il SdI. 30 giorni di prova gratuita. Ogni fattura ti mostra le tasse.

key_messages.headline: Benvenuto in Fakturo: crea la tua prima fattura
key_messages.body: Bastano pochi minuti: emetti la prima fattura elettronica e guarda la stima delle tasse aggiornarsi. Poi prova a fotografare uno scontrino e a esportare i dati per il tuo commercialista. Hai 30 giorni di prova gratuita per scoprire tutto.

content_ideas: Short screen-recorded demo video showing the tax estimate updating live as a first invoice is created, cut for Instagram Reels and LinkedIn
Co-branded webinar 'Forfettario: capire le tasse e fatturare al SdI' with professional associations, with a 30-day free trial code for members
One-page printed and PDF leaflet for accountants to hand to flat-rate clients, explaining the accountant export and the free trial
SEO guide series on e-invoicing to the SdI and how the flat-rate regime tax is estimated, each ending with a free trial call to action
Search ad campaign on flat-rate invoicing and e-invoice keywords, with landing page leading with the annual plan at 90 euros (7.50 euros per month)
Instagram carousel 'Da fattura a stima delle tasse in 3 passaggi' covering invoice, SdI sending and running estimate
Five-email onboarding sequence over the 30-day trial: first invoice, receipt photo capture, accountant export, reading the tax estimate, trial end and plan choice
LinkedIn posts addressed to freelancers on the topic 'Quanto dovrò di tasse?', linking to the trial
campaign.visual_direction: Clean, friendly and reassuring fintech look, away from the heavy tone of tax paperwork. Main colours: deep navy for trust, a fresh green for the tax estimate figure, warm off-white backgrounds, with a bright accent colour for calls to action. Hero visual: a phone showing an invoice with a large tax estimate number that ticks up, shot over real freelancer settings (a desk, a studio, a café table) across Italian cities. Rounded sans-serif typography with large, legible numbers. Simple UI close-ups on the invoice, SdI sent status, receipt photo and accountant export. Packaging and app store cues: the Fakturo logo with the tagline, and a clear '30 giorni gratis' badge. No claims about F24 payment appear anywhere in the visuals.

issues.message: The market overview states as fact that competitors cover F24 payments. This rests on ForfettApp's own marketing page and a personal blog (cristianiovino.com, S13). A data_quality_note admits it was not checked whether they offer in-app payment or only storage and submission by an accountant. The overview should soften the statement, or it should cite a stronger source such as Fiscozen's own plan page (S12). Evidence: analysis.market_overview = "Some competitors, such as ForfettApp and Fiscozen, already cover F24 payments [S11, S13]"

No cited source (S3, S4, S6) mentions a need for data migration among flat-rate freelancers who already use an app. This is an assumption presented as a segment need. Remove it, label it as a hypothesis, or support it with a source. Evidence: analysis.segments[SEG2].needs = "Easy data migration"

The analysis says Fatture in Cloud already has a Forfettari plan aimed at flat-rate freelancers (4 euros a month in year 1, 8 after). ForfettApp is also focused on the flat-rate regime and offers F24, and Fiscozen covers flat-rate users too. 'Built for flat-rate freelancers' is therefore not a clear difference. The only real differentiator is the live tax estimate. Even for that, the analysis does not check whether these competitors offer a tax estimate. Rebuild the contrast around the running tax estimate. Say plainly that the estimate has not been compared with ForfettApp or Fiscozen. Or drop the claim that Fakturo is flat-rate-specific in a way Fatture in Cloud is not. Evidence: strategy.positioning_statement = "Unlike Fatture in Cloud, it is built for flat-rate freelancers and is not a broad small-business suite."

The document says Kasa is talking to only two associations, one for designers and one for IT consultants. The analysis has no data on how many flat-rate freelancers without an app belong to them. Accountant referrals are also an untested route. Accountants often bundle their own software, so they compete with Fakturo. The two main channels meant to reach SEG1 therefore have unproven reach. The 12,000-customer goal rests mostly on search and social, and the channel plan does not show that. Add an estimate of reach by channel, or say that these channels mainly serve the partnership goal. Evidence: strategy.channels = "Professional associations"

The 'Accountant referrals' channel is reached through the commercialista, who hands the message to their flat-rate clients (see the leaflet idea). The copy is written to the freelancer ('il tuo commercialista', 'emetti', 'esporti'). It gives the accountant no reason to recommend Fakturo, such as clean exports, less data-chasing or fewer errors. Add a version for the accountant, or word the copy so it works when the accountant hands it over. Make the accountant-export benefit the lead, not the freelancer's tax estimate. Evidence: campaign.key_messages[1].body = "Con Fakturo emetti le fatture elettroniche, fotografi gli scontrini e vedi la stima delle tasse del regime forfettario."
